title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
description: Use Parameter Store for configuration values and compare it with Secrets Manager.

data.text: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store is a managed configuration store. It is simpler and cheaper than Secrets Manager, making it ideal for non-sensitive configuration values and connection strings that do not require rotation.

items: **SecureString** — encrypted values using the default AWS KMS key

data.title: Get a parameter value

rows: Paid per secret and API call

data.title: Use both
data.text: Many AWS apps use Parameter Store for configuration and Secrets Manager for sensitive secrets. The same AWS SDK credential chain works for both.

data.title: Store a feature flag in Parameter Store
data.description: Move a configuration value from appsettings.json into Parameter Store.
steps: Read the parameter in Program.cs and use it in a middleware or controller
Test that changing the parameter value changes app behavior without redeployment
data.expectedOutcome: The feature flag is read from Parameter Store and can be changed without redeploying.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Parameter Store is a simple key-value store for configuration
Secrets Manager is better for sensitive data with rotation needs
Both services use the same AWS SDK credential chain
data.takeaway: Parameter Store is the lightweight alternative to Secrets Manager for non-sensitive configuration.
